methodological_rigor.justification: Phase III RCT (CheckMate 743) 5-year follow-up of nivolumab + ipilimumab vs. chemotherapy in unresectable pleural mesothelioma. Randomization 1:1 with stratification. Long-term follow-up (median 66.8 months) enables mature OS assessment. Sensitivity analyses including treatment-switching adjustment (rank-preserving structural failure time method) appropriately address crossover. Biomarker analyses (M-MDSC levels) add mechanistic insight. Pre-specified endpoints with appropriate statistical analysis.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Phase III RCT (LoE 1b) demonstrating long-term OS benefit (5-year rates 14% vs. 6%, HR 0.74). Establishes nivolumab + ipilimumab as standard first-line therapy for unresectable mesothelioma. High clinical impact with direct implications for treatment guidelines and patient outcomes.

reporting_quality.justification: Phase III RCT with CONSORT-compliant reporting. Long-term follow-up data comprehensively reported with Kaplan-Meier curves, hazard ratios, and confidence intervals. Sensitivity analyses addressing treatment switching transparently reported. Biomarker subset analyses appropriately qualified as exploratory. Data sharing not explicitly stated but trial size and detail support reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: Long-term follow-up of previously reported CheckMate 743 trial. Maturation of OS data and biomarker subgroup analysis provide confirmatory evidence but no new mechanism or therapeutic approach.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized presentation of long-term trial outcomes with clear summary of efficacy and safety. Figures effectively communicate survival curves and biomarker subgroups. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings relative to mesothelioma standards of care. Publication-ready.

key_strengths: Phase III RCT demonstrating durable long-term OS benefit with nivolumab + ipilimumab (5-year OS 14% vs. 6% for chemotherapy)
Mature 66.8-month median follow-up enables reliable assessment of late recurrence and durability
Sensitivity analyses including treatment-switching adjustment (RPSFTM) appropriately address high crossover and confirm robustness of OS benefit
Biomarker analysis (M-MDSC levels) provides mechanistic insight into responder characteristics
Consistent benefit across tumor histologies (epithelioid, biphasic, sarcomatoid) supports broad applicability
key_concerns: Open-label design with potential for bias in follow-up care and subsequent therapy selection for control arm
High crossover in chemotherapy arm (24% received subsequent immunotherapy), potentially underestimating treatment effect despite adjustment
Biomarker subset analyses are exploratory without pre-specification; M-MDSC finding requires prospective validation
Limited mechanistic understanding of why nivolumab + ipilimumab provides durable benefit in mesothelioma despite typically immunologically 'cold' tumors
Data sharing not explicitly mentioned; raw data availability for meta-analyses not confirmed
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 2 assignment reflects mature phase III RCT with durable OS benefit establishing standard of care. Open-label design and confirmatory (rather than novel) nature preclude Tier 1 consideration.
